boardStatus.status: This is a real institution-specific one-year post-residency clinical academic general-neurology fellowship, not a primary residency, combined adult-child residency, or ABPN-recognized subspecialty certification. ABPN lists recognized subspecialty exams separately. No separate Comprehensive Neurology board exam or credential was identified. The official RCPSC page describes a primary Neurology (adult and pediatric) certification examination, with written and applied components; it is not a fellowship-specific examination.
boardStatus.blueprintScope: Mapped to ABPN Neurology Certification Content Specifications for initial certification, posted 2025-12-16: 400 questions, 80% adult/20% child and two interrelated dimensions (neurologic topics and competencies/mechanisms). Unit mapping is educational, not a weighting equivalence.
boardStatus.eligibilityContext: MGB requires an ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited neurology residency graduate, primary ABPN/RCPSC certification or eligibility, and full Massachusetts license eligibility. ABPN eligibility separately depends on current board requirements. This course does not establish eligibility.
boardStatus.separateFellowshipExam: No separate Comprehensive Neurology fellowship exam was found. ABPN primary Neurology certification is a separate board exam; RCPSC separately describes a primary Neurology (adult and pediatric) written plus applied certification exam. Neither source identifies a board exam specific to this MGB fellowship. Subspecialty exams have distinct eligibility rules.

boardEligibilityNotice: Independent self-study does not provide a medical degree, accredited residency/fellowship, supervision, competence, licensure, board eligibility, procedure authorization, or certification. Programme applicant requirements do not become course credentials. Verify current rules with ABPN/RCPSC and the programme; no passing outcome is promised.

boardStatus: A formal UCNS subspecialty certification exam exists. The official UCNS page checked 2026-10-07 lists a 4-hour, 200-question exam and a 2026 exam schedule; biennial even-year administration is stated. The separate ABHM website describes a written plus oral/practical exam and expressly says ABHM is not recognized by ABMS. UCNS and ABHM are different credentials. Headache Medicine is not a standalone ABPN primary specialty board.
boardEligibilityNotice: Educational course completion confers no exam eligibility. Current UCNS criteria (updated 2025-12-11) require primary board certification by ABMS/RCPSC/AOA (with specified alternate faculty pathway), unrestricted active physician licensure, and one of UCNS-defined pathways. Its accredited fellowship pathway requires successfully completing a >=12-month UCNS-accredited headache fellowship and applying within stated limits. The BWH page says its own applicants need an ACGME/RCPSC-accredited residency, primary ABMS/RCPSC board certified/eligible and Massachusetts licensure. Confirm current criteria directly with the certifier; no eligibility promise.
